title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 29-30
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 29 to 30 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'सुभुजो दुर्धरो वाग्मी महेन्द्रो वसुदो वसुः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 29 to 30 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 29 to 30.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 29 to 30** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **सुभुजो दुर्धरो वाग्मी महेन्द्रो वसुदो वसुः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**सुभुजो दुर्धरो वाग्मी महेन्द्रो वसुदो वसुः । नैकरूपो बृहद्रूपः शिपिविष्टः प्रकाशनः ॥** **ओजस्तेजोद्युतिधरः प्रकाशात्मा प्रतापनः । ऋद्धः स्पष्टाक्षरो मन्त्रश्चन्द्रांशुर्भास्करद्युतिः ॥**

Beautiful-armed, of a might hard to bear, sweet of speech is he. Mahendra, the giver of wealth and wealth itself, is that God of gods. Of many forms, of a vast form, he lights up the world. He bears vigour and radiance. A shining Self who warms the world is that God of gods. Rich, of clear syllables, he is the mantra, the moonbeam and the glow of the Sun.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 29 to 30 mean?
faq.a: Beautiful-armed, of a might hard to bear, sweet of speech is he. Mahendra, the giver of wealth and wealth itself, is that God of gods. Of many forms, of a vast form, he lights up the world. He bears vigour and radiance. A shining Self who warms the world is that God of gods. Rich, of clear syllables, he is the mantra, the moonbeam and the glow of the Sun.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
